To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of dijet triggers in pp collisions allows for selection of events with central collisions and a large number of hard scatterings, where the strength of the gluon field is close to the unitarity limit.

a trigger on dijets with transverse momenta above 50 GeV and pseudorapidity below 1.5 would allow to select a sample of events in which most of the protons are in central collisions, and in which the gluon field in the central region is approaching the unitarity limit.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physics of strong QCD interactions at the LHC energies, which are not yet well understood.
the development of new techniques for the study of QCD and new physics in the central region of pp collisions.
the physics of strong fields and the physics of the TeV-scale.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dijet trigger is an excellent tool for studying the physics of strong fields in QCD and for searching for new particles at the LHC.
a trigger on dijets in the central region is a powerful tool for studying the dynamics of hard parton interactions and new heavy particles at LHC.
the trigger on dijet production at LHC will allow to study the physics of strong QCD fields in a new way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a trigger on dijets at low rapidities is a powerful tool for studying hard QCD and new physics in the LHC environment.
the trigger on hard dijets is a powerful tool for studying QCD at LHC energies.
the dijet trigger is the most promising way to study the gluon fields in the central collisions, and to search for new particles, at the LHC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the physics at LHC will be very different from the physics at Tevatron.
hard processes at small rapidities provide a new, complementary approach to the study of the QCD matter at high energy density.
the physics of central events is not the same as the physics of minimum bias events.
